hero.heading: Independent vs Vendor-Led Consulting: Getting Aviation IT Procurement Right
hero.summary: When airlines and airports procure technology, they often rely on advice from vendors, systems integrators or technology resellers — all of whom have commercial relationships that influence their recommendations. This guide explains why independent advisory produces better outcomes and what to look for in an aviation technology consultant.

sections.heading: The Conflict of Interest Problem
sections.body: Vendor-led advisory — whether from a PSS provider, systems integrator, technology reseller or implementation partner — carries an inherent conflict of interest. The advisor's commercial interests are aligned with selling their product or services, not with finding the best solution for your airline or airport. This conflict manifests in subtle ways: requirements are defined to favour the vendor's product; evaluation criteria are weighted to produce a predetermined outcome; contract terms are presented as standard when they are negotiable; and implementation risks are downplayed to close the deal. Airlines and airports that rely on vendor-led advisory often discover these conflicts only after the contract is signed — when it is too late to change course without significant cost and disruption.

sections.heading: What Independent Advisory Means in Practice
sections.body: An independent aviation technology consultant has no commercial relationship with any vendor. Their fee is paid by the client — the airline or airport — and their advice is driven entirely by the client's requirements. Independence means: requirements are defined to reflect the client's actual operational and commercial needs, not a vendor's feature list; evaluation criteria are designed to identify the best solution, not to justify a predetermined choice; contract terms are reviewed to protect the client's interests, not the vendor's; and implementation risks are assessed honestly, not minimised to close a deal. AeroExpert is an independent aviation technology consultancy based in the UAE. We have no vendor relationships, no implementation revenue and no commercial incentive to recommend one solution over another.

sections.heading: The Benefits of Independent vs Vendor Consultants for Airline IT
sections.body: The benefits of independent aviation IT consulting are most visible in three areas: requirements definition, vendor evaluation and contract negotiation. Independent requirements definition produces requirements that reflect the airline's actual needs — not a vendor's feature list. This means the evaluation is based on what the airline actually needs, not what the vendor wants to sell. Independent vendor evaluation produces a defensible, auditable outcome that can withstand scrutiny from the airline's board, auditors and regulators. Vendor-led evaluation produces an outcome that is difficult to defend because the process was designed to reach a predetermined conclusion. Independent contract negotiation produces contract terms that protect the airline's interests — including SLA remedies, data portability, exit provisions and liability caps. Vendor-led contract review produces terms that protect the vendor's interests.

sections.heading: When to Use Independent Advisory
sections.body: Independent advisory is most valuable for high-stakes, long-term technology decisions — PSS selection, DCS replacement, EFB implementation, airport system procurement, cybersecurity assessments and digital transformation programmes. These are decisions that will affect the airline or airport for seven to ten years or more. The cost of independent advisory is small relative to the value of the contract being negotiated and the risk of making the wrong decision. AeroExpert advises airlines and airports in the UAE, GCC and Middle East on technology procurement across the full range of aviation systems.

sections.heading: What to Look for in an Aviation Technology Consultant
sections.body: When selecting an aviation technology consultant, look for: genuine independence (no vendor relationships, no implementation revenue); deep aviation domain expertise (not generic IT consulting applied to aviation); regional knowledge (understanding of the UAE and Middle East regulatory environment and vendor landscape); and a track record of delivering outcomes for clients, not vendors.
